response.sql: WITH txn AS (SELECT ft.transaction_amount AS amt, c.state_county_province AS state FROM Financial_Transactions ft JOIN Invoices i ON i.invoice_number = ft.invoice_number JOIN Orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id), state_totals AS (SELECT state, COALESCE(SUM(amt), 0) AS total FROM txn GROUP BY state), shares AS (SELECT state, total, total * 1.0 / SUM(total) OVER () AS share FROM state_totals), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares) SELECT SUM(s.total) AS combined_total, AVG(s.share) AS average_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS average_excess_over_avg_share FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share;

assumptions.assumption: Transactions with a NULL invoice_number are dropped by the inner joins. Invoices.order_id and Orders.customer_id are NOT NULL, so every remaining transaction resolves to a customer.
Only a NULL state_county_province counts as 'no state recorded'; NULL states form one group via GROUP BY.
Missing transaction_amount values are skipped in the sums; a state whose amounts are all missing gets a total of 0 and still counts as a state in the share average.
State values are compared exactly as stored, so blank or whitespace-only strings form their own state rather than being merged with the missing-state group.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat blank or whitespace-only state values the same as missing, so they join the no-state group.
alternatives.sql: WITH txn AS (SELECT ft.transaction_amount AS amt, NULLIF(TRIM(c.state_county_province), '') AS state FROM Financial_Transactions ft JOIN Invoices i ON i.invoice_number = ft.invoice_number JOIN Orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id), state_totals AS (SELECT state, COALESCE(SUM(amt), 0) AS total FROM txn GROUP BY state), shares AS (SELECT state, total, total * 1.0 / SUM(total) OVER () AS share FROM state_totals), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares) SELECT SUM(s.total) AS combined_total, AVG(s.share) AS average_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS average_excess_over_avg_share FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share;
